controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by HAT-P-11; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured colour.
controls.notes: No image or colour of HAT-P-11 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the colour of hat-p-11's light, as its colour lens measures it.

controls.label: Illustration
controls.qualification: NASA's artist's concept of HAT-P-11 b, from Eyes on Exoplanets; not an observation.
controls.notes: NASA's artist's concept of HAT-P-11 b: the map its Eyes on Exoplanets app wraps around the planet. Nobody has resolved this planet's disc, so none of the colour, clouds or terrain in it was observed. Its longitudes are arbitrary.

charts.alt: The orbits of HAT-P-11's planets in this map from above, to scale, with HAT-P-11 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

HAT-P-11 b's transmission spectrum: the fraction of starlight the planet blocks as it crosses its star, larger where its atmosphere absorbs. 36 measured bins from Fraine et al. 2014 (The Kepler Mission, Kepler CCD camera; Hubble Space Telescope satellite, Wide Field Camera 3; Spitzer Space Telescope satellite, Infrared Array Camera (IRAC)), as the NASA Exoplanet Archive lists them. Horizontal bars are wavelength bins; vertical bars are the published 1-sigma errors.

HAT-P-11 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (76, 82, 83) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 28230919, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 9-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.

physical.credit: Radius from Basilicata et al. 2024 (2024A&A...686A.127B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; mass from Basilicata et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024A&A...686A.127B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive; orbit from An et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169...22A), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive
